{"lens":"SAFETY_BYPASS","slice":"024B-core","reviewer":"sonnet-r2-safety_bypass","round":2,"verdict":"APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS","summary":"After fix-rounds 1+2 (closing 1 CRIT + 10 MAJ across all lenses), the SAFETY_BYPASS surface on 024B-core is substantially reduced. Bootstrap-only guard fires exit 1 at line 48-50, before any exit-2 path. Path normalisation via readlink -f / os.path.realpath precedes the denylist; macOS /private/var/* canonicalisation is Darwin-gated and tested. The --patch -- <path> approach for branch_log_modified detection (fix-round-1, closing SAFE-MAJ-002) limits diff scope to the specific log file and eliminates phantom-entry injection via other files; the rename scenario is further blocked by the [ -f \"$BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG\" ] existence check at line 123, which exits 2 if the log is absent from the working tree. Exactly-one-match assertions on cascade-status (Python re.findall) and log-entry target (parse_entry_repo) resist multi-occurrence and phantom-target injection; test cases 15, 15c, and 17 verify the exact failure modes. Template permissions are confirmed contents:read + statuses:write only; no id-token:write or attestations:write; fork-PR if: clause present and tested in assert_wrapper_contract. Adopter-slug canonicalisation converts jrnb2024/repo.foo_bar to jrnb2024-repo-foo-bar; re.escape(slug) prevents regex injection. SAFE-nit-001 (duplicate chars in parse_entry_repo branch class) and SAFE-nit-002 (missing test for identical unindented duplicate cascade-status lines) are confirmed fixed. Three carry-forward findings from R1 remain open: one MAJ (not applicable carve-out technically unguarded for cohort slices) and two MIN (slug-collision surface undocumented; dispatch-note and status-md accept out-of-repo symlinks). No new findings at CRIT or MAJ level. The open MAJ prevents fixpoint under the 0 CRIT + 0 MAJ criterion.","findings":[{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"Carry-forward from R1, unfixed. cascade-status: not applicable exits 0 with zero enforcement. No technical guard prevents a cohort cascade slice (024C-F) from declaring this value; all three enforcement checks (log-entry present, target-repo match, TF-reference regex) are bypassed. CI exits 0 with a success-class stdout message indistinguishable from a legitimate tooling-slice pass.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:144-150 — not applicable branch prints 'OK: ... not a cohort cascade slice — nothing to enforce' and exits 0 before target_repo extraction, branch_log_modified check, or TF-reference validation fire. Verified unchanged vs r3-archive/r1-safety_bypass.json. Test case 15b confirms exit 0 even with STATUS.md and DISPATCH-NOTE carrying other cascade-status artefacts.","impact":"A 024C-F DISPATCH-NOTE declaring cascade-status: not applicable (e.g. copied from 024B-core DISPATCH-NOTE without update) passes CI. enable-required-check.sh invocation-log entry never required; target-repo never verified; TF-reference check never fires. The primary branch-protection audit trail can be silently omitted; single-operator self-review (D-031) is the sole compensating guard.","mitigation":"Add --slice-type cohort|tooling flag to the CLI; reject not applicable when --slice-type cohort is passed. 024B-extras workflow wiring must pass --slice-type cohort for 024C-F jobs. Alternatively require a co-located slice-type: tooling declaration in DISPATCH-NOTE so the parser can enforce exactly-one-tooling-declaration in parallel with exactly-one-cascade-status, making careless copy-paste detectable at CI."},{"id":"SAFE-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"Carry-forward from R1, unfixed. canonicalize_adopter_slug collapses '.', '_', and runs of hyphens to '-', producing identical slugs for repos that differ only in non-alphanumeric separators (e.g. owner/a-b and owner/a.b both yield owner-a-b). A pre-existing TF-024X-renovate row for an earlier adopter falsely satisfies the STATUS.md check for a new adopter whose slug collides.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:93-99 — re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]+','-',...) merges all non-alphanumeric/non-hyphen chars uniformly. D-044 claims 'adopter-slug canonicalisation per plan-doc spec' without documenting collision exclusion. Current 5-cohort produces no collision; constraint is undocumented and untested for future adopters.","impact":"For the current 5-cohort no collision is exploitable. For future estate expansion a new adopter whose canonical slug matches an onboarded adopter's slug passes onboarded-operator-bump STATUS.md check against the prior adopter's TF row, allowing CI to pass silently without a distinct TF-024X-renovate row for the new adopter.","mitigation":"Document the slug-uniqueness constraint explicitly in D-044 and the canonicalize_adopter_slug function. At adoption time assert the new adopter's canonical slug is absent from existing TF-024X- rows in STATUS.md and branch-protection-log.md. For long-term robustness consider appending a short stable hash suffix to disambiguate structurally similar repo names."},{"id":"SAFE-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"Carry-forward from R1, unfixed. --dispatch-note and --status-md are normalised with os.path.normpath (resolves ./ and ../ segments only, does NOT resolve symlinks), while --branch-protection-log receives os.path.realpath plus an explicit repo-root containment check. A symlink passed as --dispatch-note or --status-md pointing outside the repository is silently followed.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:89-95 — normalize_path() calls os.path.normpath. Lines 110-114 apply os.path.realpath + repo-root case check only to BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG_REAL. No equivalent containment assertion for DISPATCH_NOTE or STATUS_MD. Verified unchanged vs r3-archive/r1-safety_bypass.json.","impact":"An operator passing --status-md pointing via symlink to an external file containing a TF-024X-renovate-<slug> regex match would produce a false-positive pass for onboarded-operator-bump. In practice the TF regex is unlikely to match arbitrary files (fail-closed tendency), but the asymmetric trust treatment is a hardening gap and a minor D-044 trust-model inaccuracy regarding path containment.","mitigation":"Apply os.path.realpath + repo-root containment check to --dispatch-note and --status-md consistently with --branch-protection-log. The REPO_ROOT realpath computation at lines 105-109 is directly reusable; the containment case-pattern and die path already exist for --branch-protection-log and can be copied verbatim for the other two inputs."}]}
